claims.text: This dispute is safety-flagged, and the safety indicator is on the face of the chat log rather than merely in the rider's claim: at 21:40:10 the driver wrote 'Wah your profile photo very pretty leh, got bf or not? Give me your number', and the rider answered at 21:41:00 'That's inappropriate. I'm not getting in your car.' Inappropriate conduct toward a rider and a rider who felt unsafe to board are precisely the POL-GEN-21 triggers, so this case must go to human review whatever category was chosen, the AI may not rule on it or recommend a resolution, and under POL-GEN-03 an escalated amount is held - the SGD 5.00 stays uncollected pending that review instead of standing as a charge against the rider.

The no-show finality rule does not rescue the fee here. POL-NS-26 makes an AI no-show ruling final only 'subject to POL-GEN-21 (safety)', and POL-GEN-22's finality for a dispute below SGD 10.00 is subject to the same carve-out. With the safety flag set and the driver's conduct recorded in the log, neither finality provision applies and the 5.00 SGD fee cannot be fixed by an AI ruling on this record; the outcome is escalation with the amount held.

POL-NS-22 licenses DRIVER_COMPENSATION only 'where the fee stands'. A fee held on an open safety escalation does not stand, so no compensation to the driver can issue out of this record. The fare ledger shows the 5.00 SGD charged at 21:43:14 with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and payment_status CHARGED - that is the state that should be preserved as held, not affirmed as a completed no-show.

The fee was applied with actual notice that the rider was not boarding and why. The chat log shows MSG-06063-004 was delivered at 21:41:01 and read at 21:41:17, and the driver cancelled at 21:43:10 - almost two minutes after reading 'That's inappropriate. I'm not getting in your car.' The driver's counter-account ('Only friendly chat. Passenger didn't come, so I cancel.') does not engage with that notice, so the record does not establish the clean rider no-show that POL-NS-22's fee presupposes; the contested footing of the fee is a matter for the human reviewer under POL-GEN-21.

Honest concession: the rider does not rest on the POL-NS-23 contact obligation. The derived contact_before_cancel facts show two driver chat messages (21:37:00 and 21:40:10) and one in-app call to the rider (21:39:20, unanswered, 15 s), all before the 21:43:10 cancellation, so on this record that obligation is met and NS-23 does not by itself void the fee. The rider's case rests on the safety escalation, not on a false NS-23 point.

Nothing on the rider's side supplies an alternative ground for refusing her: rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is 0, so even if the fee were later to stand the POL-NS-25 repeat-no-show referral would not be triggered against this rider's account. That referral is unavailable here and cannot be weighed against her while the safety escalation is open.

claims.text: Every precondition of the no-show fee is made out on the platform record. The driver marked arrival at 21:36:40; the 300-second free wait therefore ran from arrival (an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, POL-NS-21) and expired at 21:41:40; the driver cancelled only at 21:43:10, i.e. 390 seconds after arrival and after the free wait had run out. The record's own derived check reports cancelled_after_free_wait true. The fee was validly incurred and the rider's claim cannot be sustained on the no-show arithmetic.

POL-NS-23's contact obligation is discharged, so there is no ground to void the fee. The driver sent in-app chat messages at 21:37:00 and 21:40:10 and placed an in-app call at 21:39:20 (ringing 15 s, unanswered), all before the 21:43:10 cancellation; the trip record's derived contact check reports obligation_met true and the chat log is contiguous and reconciles to chat_message_count. The clause requires that a message and a call be placed, not answered — both were placed.

The arrival test is satisfied: the driver-device trace's nearest fix to the pickup is 2.71 m away at 21:37:48, comfortably inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD pickup zone, and the record's arrival_check reports corroborated true on a clean trace (25 fixes at 30 s, max gap 30 s, 100% coverage, every fix reporting accuracy within 9 m). The driver was at the pickup, so POL-NS-24's driver-no-show ground does not arise.

The amount charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD the schedule fixes, and the payments ledger carries a single cancellation-fee line that reconciles to total_charged, with refund_issued_sgd 0.0. On the merits, the ruling this fee calls for is DRIVER_COMPENSATION under POL-NS-22, with both amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd at 5.00 SGD.

The dispute is flagged safety-related and its own claim narrates inappropriate messages and a rider who felt unsafe — heads of POL-GEN-21 that the AI may not adjudicate whatever category the filer chose. The case therefore goes to human review, and because ESCALATE holds the amount rather than moving it (POL-GEN-03), the 5.00 SGD charge is held pending that review and is not refunded by this tribunal. Escalation is the driver's protection here, not a loss: it preserves the fee that the no-show preconditions establish.

I do not press the driver's counterparty statement that the exchange was 'only friendly chat'. MSG-06063-003 at 21:40:10 plainly goes beyond arranging the pickup, and the rider's 21:41:00 reply marks it as unwelcome. That disagreement is precisely the factual question POL-GEN-21 reserves for the human reviewer; it does not disturb the arrival, free-wait and contact facts that carry the fee, none of which depends on the content of the messages.

Disclosure: the only impaired artifact in the bundle is the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-06063-01, which is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) and carries weight 0.0. No no-show clause makes a traffic advisory a precondition of the fee, and POL-GEN-26 escalates only where a rule needs a fact the record cannot establish — no such fact is outstanding here, since arrival, wait and contact are all carried by COMPLETE, full-weight artifacts. Its absence leaves the fee untouched.
